extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational-linguistics researchers and practitioners working on computational humor and humor recognition
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating deep-learning models (CNNs with highway networks) for automatic humor recognition, using collected multilingual datasets of distinct joke types and standard classification metrics. Includes benchmarking against prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Results show that our model outperforms in recognition of different types of humor with benchmarks collected in both English and Chinese languages on accuracy, precision, and recall in comparison to previous works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall) to evaluate humor-recognition models and compare against prior benchmarks across languages and joke types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset construction: four datasets with distinct joke types in English and Chinese
rubrics_metrics.description: We construct and collect four datasets with distinct joke types in both English and Chinese and conduct learning experiments on humor recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design datasets that cover multiple, distinct joke types and include multilingual (English and Chinese) examples to test model generality across joke forms and languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model architecture: CNN with extensive filter sizes/numbers and Highway Networks
rubrics_metrics.description: We implement a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with extensive filter size, number and Highway Networks to increase the depth of networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ convolutional architectures with varied filter sizes and counts; use Highway Networks (or similar mechanisms) to allow deeper network training for improved feature extraction in humor recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition across different types of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct learning experiments on humor recognition across different joke types (distinct joke-type datasets) to assess model ability to handle diverse humor structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate models not only on aggregate metrics but per joke-type to identify strengths/weaknesses on different humor phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking and comparison to previous works
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare model performance against previous works; the paper reports outperforming prior methods on the collected benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include baselines from prior literature and present comparative results (e.g., metric-by-metric) to demonstrate improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader research goals: discovering humor structures, recognition, and generation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to build computational models to discover the structures of humor, recognize humor and even generate humor remains a challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame work within the broader aims of computational humor: analysis of humor structure, supervised recognition tasks, and potential extension to humor generation; justify dataset/model choices in light of these goals.
